message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to very different modern orders—Carnivora for the lion and Perissodactyla for the zebra—but they do share a common ancestor at the level of the class **Mammalia**. Their last common ancestor was a small, shrew‑like mammal that lived roughly **70 million years ago** during the Paleocene epoch. From that point onward, the lineages that would become carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates diverged, eventually giving rise to the diverse groups we see today.
